sections.title: 1 Event — Cross-checking the Flight 15 '11/13 double catch' reports against primary sources
sections.html:
ItemValue (checked 2026-11-10)Source grade · source
LL2 launch recordNET 2026-11-13 22:45 UTC · status 'To Be Confirmed' · window end 2026-11-14 00:00 UTC · last updated 2026-11-09 23:06 UTC · Orbital Launch Pad 2 (Starbase). Mission description (pre-launch planning wording): first attempt at second-stage return to the launch site · booster tower catch④ LL2 upcoming · data/spacex_watch.json launches.starship_next (11/10 08:31 KST, same date and status)
Origin of the dateSpaceX launch vice president Dontchev (UP.Summit) gave 11/13. The earlier FAA flight plan slide went from 11/8 → 11/12 — it is a regulator planning date, not a company date⑥ Teslarati 11/05 (citing Ars Technica)
HardwareBooster 22 33-engine static fire (10/25) · Ship 42 6-engine static fire of about 60 seconds (around 10/27) — same as the November issue and the 11/9 run record (no change)⑥ Teslarati 11/05 · state.triggers_next_12m[T3].status
FAA licenseIssuance of a modified Flight 15 license is not confirmed — reports say the Flight 14 license covered only that flight, and that a modification is needed to include the Ship's return to the launch site (flight over densely populated areas). The FAA Starship page returned 403 in this run⑤ NASASpaceflight November (title and search summary — body 403) · FAA Starship (403)
FilingsNo SpaceX 8-K or IR release — latest on EDGAR is the 11/06 8-K (Item 5.02); latest on IR RSS is 11/06① EDGAR filing list · ② IR RSS, accessed 2026-11-10

Verdict: The content of the two watcher reports (11/13 · simultaneous booster + Ship catch) is the same as the T3 record in the 11/9 run. The only new confirmation is that LL2 kept the date as of the evening of 11/9 (UTC), and the remaining uncertainty (the license) is unchanged. Since this is a confirmation, not an event, there is no milestone or probability input — B-2027-1 (start of Ship recovery and reuse) and R2 move only once the flight result is out. The measurement layer LL2 will automatically detect it as a 'flight with confirmed result' (launch_final), and that opens the next event run (Source: table above · state.probability_adjustment_rules R2 · state.milestones B-2027-1).

Measurement layer's share (listing only): The watcher woke the engine again with a repeat report of the same trigger and the same date. The judgment layer had nothing to do — a rule not to wake it for a 'repeat report of a date already recorded' is left in open_questions_for_next_run as a measurement-layer design task (Source: data/spacex_watch.json due).
